work.name: Universidad Adventista del Plata, Systems Development Department
highlights: SIED platform: took part in developing the institutional training platform (enrollment, payments, coupons, Moodle sync), in PHP 8.2 with layered Controllers, Services, Repositories and Entities, on PostgreSQL and Docker.

Secure file handling: built the flow for the documents each plan requires. Every file is checked by its actual content, not just its extension, stored outside the public part of the server, and only its owner or an administrator can download it.

Database migration testing: own regression and SQL-compatibility testing of 3 legacy systems for the migration of their PostgreSQL database. Built a 65-item functional inventory verified against the codebase, surfacing implicit integer casts, collation-sensitive ORDER BY and UNION type mismatches.

projects.name: EmprendER: Entrepreneurship platform
highlights: Built the four-step entrepreneur registration, including a generic server-action validator parameterized by schema and redirect per step; the entrepreneurship module (upload limits, deactivation and its endpoints); the posts CMS (Prisma model, rich-text editor, markdown modal); and authentication and session handling. Reviewed and merged teammates' pull requests.

Production readiness: responsible for development since the codebase moved to the university's self-hosted GitLab: unified Zod validation, isolated JWT handling, and a systematic React correctness sweep over roughly a dozen screens (hook-rule violations, setState inside effects, unstable dependency arrays, server-side session hydration), plus toolchain modernization (Prisma v6, pnpm, ESLint flat config, the Next.js 16 middleware-to-proxy move).

Security and testing: tested the app and patched what I found, such as the /api/admin/* routes, which only checked in the browser whether the user was an administrator and now check on the server too. Built the test suite from scratch (Playwright coverage for all three roles plus an 8-test smoke tier on every push), which immediately surfaced a login endpoint returning 500 instead of 401 on bad credentials.

projects.name: MTDS: Laparoscopic surgery training robot
roles: Control software and simulation, university research project
highlights: Kinematics and firmware: wrote the arm's motion layer in C++, with closed-form analytic inverse kinematics validated against the CAD model and tool-space resolved-rate control, unit tested and warning-clean.

Research: we studied whether the planned software Remote Center of Motion could work on the built arm. Five independent numerical checks showed it could not (it was two degrees of freedom short), so we changed the direction of development in time, toward a structural fix that reaches all four laparoscopic degrees of freedom with no extra motors.

Simulation and tooling: built a browser 3D simulator so the team and the client can operate the arm without hardware, and automated the Fusion 360 assembly and measurement work through its Python API.
